title.ja: Verb る ことになる

explanation.en: Used to express that something has been decided or arranged, often indicating a decision made by someone else or due to circumstances.
explanation.ja: 何かが決定または手配されたことを表現します。通常、他の人によって決まったり、状況により決められたことを示します。

components.explanation: Indicates that something has been decided or arranged.
examples: 決定された (kettei sareta) - It was decided

examples.japanese: 今日は会議がなくなることになりました。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa kaigi ga nakunaru koto ni narimashita.
examples.english: It has been decided that there will be no meeting today.

breakdown.なくなることになります: nakunaru koto ni narimasu - it was decided to cancel

examples.japanese: 来週、友達と旅行することになった。
examples.romaji: Raishuu, tomodachi to ryokou suru koto ni natta.
examples.english: It has been arranged that I will travel with my friends next week.

breakdown.旅行することになった: ryokou suru koto ni natta - it was decided to travel

examples.japanese: 彼女が今度のプロジェクトのリーダーになることになりました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ga kondo no purojekuto no riida ni naru koto ni narimashita.
examples.english: It has been decided that she will be the leader of the next project.

breakdown.今度のプロジェクトの: kondo no purojekuto no - the next project's
breakdown.リーダーになることになりました: riida ni naru koto ni narimashita - it was decided that she would be the leader

examples.japanese: 急に仕事が入ったので、休みを取ることになった。
examples.romaji: Kyuu ni shigoto ga haitta node, yasumi wo toru koto ni natta.
examples.english: Due to sudden work, it has been decided that I will take a day off.

breakdown.急に仕事が入った: kyuu ni shigoto ga haitta - due to sudden work
breakdown.休みを取ることになった: yasumi wo toru koto ni natta - it was decided to take a break

commonMistakes.mistake: Using ことになる without a preceding verb in る form.
commonMistakes.correction: Ensure the sentence includes a verb in its dictionary (る) form before applying ことになる.
commonMistakes.example: Correct: 食べることになった。 - It was decided that I would eat.
